dct_description_sm: The goals of fieldwork all relate to establishing the extent of ground ice on Herschel Island and the northern Yukon coast to assess the impact of its thaw. Herschel Island is an extremely ice-rich permafrost landscape in delicate balance with climate change and on the verge of widespread degradation in many areas. Currently, the island is a territorial park in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region (ISR), so historic resources are protected by law. In 2007, the Worlds Monuments Fund listed Herschel Island among the top 100 most endangered historic sites in the world. Herschel Island, along with Ivvavik National Park of Canada and Ventut National Park of Canada, is also being considered as a potential UNESCO World Heritage site.
dct_title_s: Geophysical Data for Massive Ground Ice Distribution at Herschel Island, Yukon Territory
